citations.quote: The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following statement.
A **comoment map** in this page's usage is a real-linear map $J:\mathfrak g\to A$ satisfying $$J([\xi,\eta])=\{J(\xi),J(\eta)\}\qquad(\xi,\eta\in\mathfrak g).$$
The Poisson bracket is real-bilinear and skew-symmetric, and $$\{F,GH\}=\{F,G\}H+G\{F,H\},\qquad \{FG,H\}=F\{G,H\}+G\{F,H\}.$
For $F,G\in C^\infty(M)$, the **Poisson bracket** in the library convention is $$\{F,G\}:=\omega(X_F,X_G)=dF(X_G)=X_G(F)=-X_F(G).$$

The map $\mu$ is an **infinitesimal moment map** for the action when the **component moment equations** $$d\mu^\xi=-\iota_{\xi_M}\omega \qquad\text{hold for every }\xi\in\mathfrak g$$ hold; equivalently, when the map $\mathfrak g\to C^\infty(M)$, $\xi\mapsto\mu^\xi$ is linear and each $\mu^\xi$ is a Hamiltonian function for the vector field $-\xi_M$.
If $\mu$ is coadjoint equivariant, then $\{\mu^\xi,\mu^\eta\}=\mu^{[\xi,\eta]}$ on all of $M$ for all $\xi,\eta\in\mathfrak g$.
A **representation** of a Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ on $V$ is a Lie-algebra homomorphism $$\rho:\mathfrak g\longrightarrow\mathfrak{gl}(V).$$
